root_cause: an in-process cache in checkout-service grows without bound: entries are added and never evicted, so the resident set climbs and the service slows under garbage-collection pressure

evidence.observation: rose from 0.0 to 484.5, flat at zero through the baseline
evidence.supports: the cache never evicts - this is the mechanism
the resident set follows the cache, which ties the growth to it
the slowdown is a consequence of the memory pressure, not a cause

evidence.observation: stayed at 0.0 for the whole window
evidence.supports: the database pool is untouched - the fault is in the process, not in its I/O

ruled_out: connection pool exhaustion - db_pool_usage stayed at 0.0 throughout
CPU saturation - p95_by_dependency rose on both dependencies, but cache_entries went from 0 to 484.5 and memory_mb x2.41 in the same window; the latency follows the memory growth
an internal error in a dependency - no dependency_error or inventory_internal_error event appears, while cache_entries and memory_mb both rose
